BOX 25287 DENVER, COLORADO 80225-0287 File Code: A16 Sole Source Justification Park/PMIS NAMA 291052 PR Number TBD Date: March 31, 2026 Reference: Construction Services, NAMA 291052 Pool Lining Subject: Sole Source Justification Other than Full and Open Competition In accordance with FAR 6.103-2, the following information is provided:

1. Identification of the Agency and the Contracting Activity:

Department of the Interior (DOI), National Park Service (NPS), Denver Service Center (DSC), Contracting Services (CS) Division on behalf of DOI NPS DSC, Design and Construction (D&C) Division.

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved:

This action is for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract to perform concrete surface repairs and install a high-performance, fully submersible, waterproof, anti-microbial, and anti-algae polyurea coating system at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The work includes surface preparation, crack and joint repair, and installation of a multi-component Rhino Linings coating system consisting of Rhino CCW Polyurea, Rhino 11-35 Polyurea, Rhino 406 Epoxy Primer, and Rhino Pipeliner 5000, in accordance with the revised Statement of Work.

3. A Description of the Supplies or Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs, Including the Estimated Value:

The work includes the following:

• Shot blasting the pool floor to ICRI CSP 3–5 and sandblasting vertical surfaces and joints • Crack repair using manufacturer-approved sealants • Complete joint removal, cleaning, backer rod installation, and refilling with Rhino CCW Polyurea • Application of Rhino 11-35 Polyurea as the joint cap/elastic layer • Application of Rhino 406 Epoxy Primer at ~5 mils DFT • Installation of Rhino Pipeliner 5000 polyurea system to a final thickness of 100 mils ± • Sealing of the horizontal coping joint using manufacturer-approved sealants • Thickness verification, adhesion testing, and spark (holiday) testing • Mobilization from April 1–3, in-pool work beginning April 6, and substantial completion by May 22 These services are required to produce a seamless, monolithic, waterproof, antimicrobial, and anti-algae system suitable for continuous submersion.

These services are essential to restore structural durability, prevent microbial growth, ensure public-safe conditions, and maintain the integrity and appearance of a nationally significant landmark.

The IGE for this project is $10,256,576, based on historical coating-system costs, labor and material pricing for similar structural-concrete repairs, market pricing for Rhino Linings polyurea and associated system components.

JOFOC Over SAT

4. Identification of the Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition:

FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency. This authority applies when the Government’s need is of such an unusual and compelling nature that delays in award would seriously injure the Government.

FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, applies because delaying the award long enough to conduct a competitive procurement would prevent the National Park Service from completing the work in time to reopen the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool for the Nation’s 250th anniversary event series. This delay would result in serious injury to the Government, including failure to meet statutory visitor-safety responsibilities and operational commitments for the 250th.

A competitive acquisition would introduce an unavoidable 10–15-week delay for solicitation, proposal development, evaluation, and award. Such delay would push the start of construction beyond the narrow spring environmental window required for concrete curing and multi-stage coating installation. Missing this window would mean the Reflecting Pool could not be refilled and made operational for the 250th anniversary, which constitutes mission failure and exposes the Government to public-safety, resource-protection, and event-support risks.

The technical process (concrete repairs, cure cycles, pretreatment chemistry, and coating installation) can only be executed within strict temperature and humidity conditions. Any shift in schedule pushes these phases into weather conditions where the system cannot cure performance requirements, making delays unacceptable. Thus, fully competing the requirement would directly prevent the Government from executing essential operations tied to a major national commemoration, satisfying the GAO-recognized standard for “unusual and compelling urgency.” Delaying award to conduct a full and open competition would cause serious injury to the Government, as defined under FAR 6.103-2. If Government were required to conduct a traditional competitive procurement cycle estimated at 10-15 weeks the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool would not be able to reopen in time to meet the NPS’s affirmative operational obligations for the 250th anniversary commemoration.

The Reflecting Pool is a central feature of the National Mall’s visitor experience and is an essential component in NPS’s planned programming and crowd-management posture for the 250th. Failure to complete the concrete repairs and coating installation before the required curing window closes would result in the Pool remaining drained or partially inoperable during the event period. This outcome constitutes mission failure, as the NPS has explicit responsibilities for public safety, resource protection, and visitor services tied to the 250th.

The technical nature of the repairs requires strict environmental conditions and multistage curing cycles that can only occur within the narrow spring installation window. Thus, competition would directly prevent the Government from meeting a mandated, time-certain mission requirement.

5. Minimum Quantity and Why the full scope is Urgent.

The NPS evaluated whether the requirement could be divided into urgent and non-urgent components and whether a partial award could satisfy only the minimum quantity necessary to meet the immediate need.

This analysis concluded that the entire project scope is inherently urgent for the following reasons. The Rhino Linings polyurea system is an integrated, monolithic waterproofing assembly requiring continuous sequencing from joint repair through primer and polyurea installation. Phasing or partial execution is not technically feasible, would compromise adhesion and system integrity, and would void the manufacturer’s warranty. All work elements—surface preparation, crack repair, joint treatment, primer, and polyurea application—are interdependent. The environmental window for installation is limited, and dividing work would require re-staging, repeated shutdowns, and additional weather exposure, which would risk system failure and prevent timely reopening for the 250th anniversary.

Based on this evaluation, limiting the award to a minimum subset of work would fail to achieve the Government’s urgent need and would still result in operational failure during the 250th anniversary. Therefore, the full scope constitutes the minimum quantity necessary to meet the urgent mission requirement.

JOFOC Over SAT

6. A Demonstration that the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the Acquisition Requires Use of the Authority Cited. The NPS intends to award this contract to Atlantic Industrial Coating Limited Liability Company.

The contractor’s unique qualifications include: The work requires a contractor with demonstrated experience installing Rhino Linings multi-component polyurea systems, including joint fillers, elastic joint-cap membranes, epoxy primers, and high-build (100 mil ±) polyurea waterproofing applied using heated plural-component spray equipment. The installation requires precise sequencing, temperature-controlled plural-component application, and validated capability to achieve uniform monolithic thickness without holidays, pinholes, or adhesion failures. The contractor must demonstrate the ability to perform all surface preparation, joint treatment, polyurea application, and quality-control testing required by the manufacturer for warranty compliance. Immediate mobilization capability is necessary to meet the compressed installation schedule and environmental curing requirements. The Government determined these qualifications are essential, not merely beneficial, because improper installation of any single material system results in delamination, blistering, discoloration, microbial growth, or premature failure — all of which compromise public safety and the operational readiness of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

7. A Description of Efforts Made to Ensure that Offers are Solicited from as Many Potential Sources as is Practicable, Including Whether a Notice Was or Will be Publicized as Required by FAR 5.2 and, if Not, Which Exception Under FAR 5.202 Applies: While multiple contractors may perform general concrete repair, the revised SOW requires specialized experience with thick-build polyurea systems, manufacturer-approved materials, and heated plural-component application equipment. Only a limited pool of contractors possess the qualifications and equipment necessary to install Rhino CCW Polyurea, Rhino 11-35 Polyurea, Rhino 406 Epoxy Primer, and Rhino Pipeliner 5000 as a unified system. Furthermore, the schedule constraints and strict environmental window preclude a competitive procurement cycle, as any delay would prevent project completion before May 22. Why a Competitive Cycle Cannot Meet the Timeline: 4–6 weeks for solicitation preparation and posting 3–4 weeks for proposal development 2–3 weeks for evaluation and award 1–2 weeks for GC subcontract solicitation, evaluation, and award to the system manufacturer Thus, a competitive procurement is incompatible with the critical path dictated by long-lead system fabrication.

8. A Determination by the Contracting Officer that the Anticipated Cost to the Government Will be Fair and Reasonable: The Contracting Officer has determined pricing to be fair and reasonable based on historical pricing for comparable systems, proprietary manufacturer pricing, and market research in accordance with FAR 15.401. Pricing will be evaluated by the Contracting Officer using: • Historical pricing for similar coating and repair work • Comparison with prior NPS and DOI awards of similar complexity • Market research of proprietary manufacturer pricing

9. A Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results or a Statement of the Reason Market Research Was Not Conducted:

Market research indicates that although multiple firms perform concrete preparation and repair, only a subset possesses the equipment, manufacturer affiliation, and demonstrated experience in installing multi-component JOF0C Over SAT polyurea waterproofing systems such as Rhino Pipeliner 5000. Due to the schedule constraints and required specialized material performance, full and open competition remains impracticable.

10. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other than Full and Open Competition:

Future acquisitions will benefit from early planning to allow time for complete competition cycles and expanded market engagement ahead of fixed public-event deadlines.

While multiple firms expressed interest during market research, the NPS determined that pursuing competition under the available timeline would itself prevent the NPS from meeting its mission obligations during the 250th anniversary. GAO case law requires agencies to demonstrate how delay not priority status causes injury. Here, the consequences of delay are concrete, time-bound, and unavoidable.

Competing the requirement introduces a minimum 10–15 week delay, which would: push the start of work beyond acceptable environmental conditions for concrete curing; prevent the NPS from restoring the Pool to operational status before the 250th activities commence; and create public-safety and resource-protection risks associated with an empty or partially repaired Pool during a major national event.

11. A Listing of the Sources, if any, that Expressed in Writing, an Interest in the Acquisition:

Multiple contractors expressed interest in the project, however due to the time constraints listed in above a competitive acquisition is not the best route for the Government.

12. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any Barriers to Competition Before any Subsequent Acquisition for the Supplies or Services Required:

Earlier project planning will ensure future procurements allow adequate time for full GC competition and subcontractor system sourcing.
